tasks.title: Config.copy() should return a Config, not a plain dict
tasks.prompt: `app.config.copy()` returns a plain `dict` because `Config` inherits `dict.copy`, so the copy loses `root_path` and the loading methods (`from_mapping`, `from_pyfile`, `from_object`, ...). I want to copy a config and keep using the copy as a config. Make `Config.copy()` return a shallow copy that is an instance of the same class as the original (including subclasses of `Config`), with the same `root_path` and the same keys and values. Changing the copy must not change the original. Nested values such as dicts are shared between the two, not copied.
tasks.hidden_test:
import flask


def test_copy_returns_config_instance(tmp_path):
    config = flask.Config(tmp_path, {"SECRET_KEY": "dev", "NESTED": {"a": 1}})
    copied = config.copy()

    assert type(copied) is flask.Config
    assert copied is not config
    assert copied == {"SECRET_KEY": "dev", "NESTED": {"a": 1}}
    assert copied.root_path == config.root_path


def test_copy_is_independent_and_shallow(tmp_path):
    config = flask.Config(tmp_path, {"A": 1, "NESTED": {"a": 1}})
    copied = config.copy()
    copied["B"] = 2
    copied.from_mapping(C=3)

    assert copied["B"] == 2
    assert copied["C"] == 3
    assert "B" not in config
    assert "C" not in config
    assert copied["NESTED"] is config["NESTED"]


def test_copy_preserves_subclass(tmp_path):
    class CustomConfig(flask.Config):
        pass

    config = CustomConfig(tmp_path, {"A": 1})
    copied = config.copy()

    assert type(copied) is CustomConfig
    assert copied["A"] == 1
    assert copied.root_path == tmp_path


def test_copy_app_config(app):
    copied = app.config.copy()

    assert isinstance(copied, flask.Config)
    assert copied["SECRET_KEY"] == "test key"
    assert copied.root_path == app.config.root_path

tasks.title: MethodView should respond 405 for a listed but unimplemented method
tasks.prompt: When a `MethodView` subclass lists a method in `methods` but doesn't define the matching handler (for example `methods = ["GET", "POST"]` with only a `get` method), a request with that method fails with an `AssertionError` ("Unimplemented method ..."). That becomes a 500 error, or propagates out of the test client when testing. It should be a client error instead. Raise `werkzeug.exceptions.MethodNotAllowed`, so the response is a 405 and any registered 405 error handler is used. Its valid methods, which are sent in the `Allow` header, should be the upper-case names of the HTTP methods that the view class actually defines handler methods for. Falling back from HEAD to `get` stays as it is.

tasks.title: Set session.new for the default cookie session
tasks.prompt: `session.new` is always `False` with the default signed cookie session, so a view can't tell whether the visitor arrived without a session. Make `SecureCookieSessionInterface.open_session` return a session whose `new` attribute is `True` when the request has no session cookie, or when the cookie's signature is invalid or expired, and `False` when the session was loaded from a valid cookie. This should also apply to the session yielded by the test client's `session_transaction()`.

import flask


def _add_view(app):
    @app.route("/")
    def index():
        is_new = flask.session.new
        flask.session["visits"] = flask.session.get("visits", 0) + 1
        return str(is_new)


def test_session_new_without_and_with_cookie(app, client):
    _add_view(app)

    assert client.get("/").text == "True"
    assert client.get("/").text == "False"
    assert client.get("/").text == "False"


def test_session_new_with_bad_signature(app, client):
    _add_view(app)

    assert client.get("/").text == "True"
    client.set_cookie("session", "not-a-valid-signature")
    assert client.get("/").text == "True"


def test_session_transaction_new(app, client):
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert sess.new is True
        sess["x"] = 1

    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert sess.new is False
        assert sess["x"] == 1

tasks.title: Filter `flask routes` output by endpoint prefix
tasks.prompt: In large apps the `flask routes` output is too long to scan. Add an `--endpoint` option to the `flask routes` command that takes a string. When it's given, only routes whose endpoint starts with that string are listed (for example `--endpoint api.` shows only the routes of the `api` blueprint). `--sort` and `--all-methods` keep working on the filtered list. If the app has routes but none match, print `No routes match the endpoint prefix 'VALUE'.`, with the value quoted like Python's `repr` (for example `No routes match the endpoint prefix 'nope'.`), and exit with status 0. Without the option the output is unchanged, including the existing `No routes were registered.` message for an app without routes.

tasks.title: Reject nested blueprint registrations that create a cycle
tasks.prompt: Nesting blueprints in a cycle isn't caught. After `a.register_blueprint(b)`, calling `b.register_blueprint(a)` is accepted, and registering `a` on an app later fails with a `RecursionError`. `Blueprint.register_blueprint` already rejects registering a blueprint on itself. Extend it to reject any registration that would create a cycle, whether direct or through deeper nesting (for example a -> b -> c, then `c.register_blueprint(a)`). Raise `ValueError` from the `register_blueprint` call with the message `Cannot register blueprint '<child>' on '<parent>', it would create a cycle.`, where `<child>` is the name of the blueprint being registered and `<parent>` is the name of the blueprint it is being registered on. For example: `Cannot register blueprint 'a' on 'b', it would create a cycle.` Keep the existing `Cannot register a blueprint on itself` error for the self case. Registering the same child under two different parents is not a cycle and must still work.

tasks.title: Accept a single category string in get_flashed_messages
tasks.prompt: `get_flashed_messages(category_filter=...)` is documented as taking a list of categories, but people often pass a single string such as `category_filter="error"`. That string is then checked with `in`, so any category that is a substring of it (like `"err"`) matches as well, and the wrong messages are returned. Accept a single string for `category_filter` and treat it as one category, exactly as if `["error"]` had been passed. Passing lists or tuples keeps working as before, and `with_categories` behaves the same.

def test_category_filter_single_string(app, req_ctx):
    flask.flash("a", "error")
    flask.flash("b", "err")
    flask.flash("c")

    assert flask.get_flashed_messages(category_filter="error") == ["a"]
    assert flask.get_flashed_messages(
        category_filter="err", with_categories=True
    ) == [("err", "b")]
    assert flask.get_flashed_messages(category_filter="message") == ["c"]


def test_category_filter_iterable_unchanged(app, req_ctx):
    flask.flash("a", "error")
    flask.flash("b", "warning")
    flask.flash("c")

    assert flask.get_flashed_messages(category_filter=["error", "warning"]) == [
        "a",
        "b",
    ]
    assert flask.get_flashed_messages(category_filter=("message",)) == ["c"]

tasks.title: Let the test client take default environ_base values
tasks.prompt: I want default WSGI environ values for every request made by one test client, for example `app.test_client(environ_base={"REMOTE_ADDR": "10.0.0.5"})`. Right now that raises `TypeError` because the keyword is passed on to Werkzeug's `Client`. Add an `environ_base` keyword argument to `FlaskClient` (default `None`); `app.test_client(**kwargs)` already passes extra keyword arguments to the client class. The given values are merged over the client's built-in defaults (`REMOTE_ADDR` of `127.0.0.1` and the Werkzeug `HTTP_USER_AGENT`), so defaults that are not overridden are kept. An `environ_base` passed to an individual request (such as `client.get("/", environ_base=...)`) still takes precedence over the client's values. Other clients are not affected.

tasks.title: Allow max_cookie_size to be set per response
tasks.prompt: `Response.max_cookie_size` is read-only. It always comes from the `MAX_COOKIE_SIZE` config, or Werkzeug's default of 4093 outside an app context. I'd like to raise or lower the limit for a single response, the same way `request.max_content_length` can be set per request. Make `max_cookie_size` assignable on a response instance. When it is set to an int, that value is returned (inside or outside an app context) and used when setting cookies on that response, so the "cookie is too large" warning uses the per-response limit. Assigning `None` restores the default behaviour: the config value inside an app context, Werkzeug's default outside one. Other responses are not affected.

import warnings

import pytest

import flask


def test_max_cookie_size_can_be_set(app):
    app.config["MAX_COOKIE_SIZE"] = 100
    response = flask.Response()
    response.max_cookie_size = 20

    assert response.max_cookie_size == 20

    with app.app_context():
        assert response.max_cookie_size == 20
        assert flask.Response().max_cookie_size == 100


def test_max_cookie_size_reset_to_default(app):
    app.config["MAX_COOKIE_SIZE"] = 100
    response = flask.Response()
    response.max_cookie_size = 20
    response.max_cookie_size = None

    assert response.max_cookie_size == flask.Flask.default_config["MAX_COOKIE_SIZE"]

    with app.app_context():
        assert response.max_cookie_size == 100


def test_max_cookie_size_used_for_warning():
    response = flask.Response()
    response.max_cookie_size = 10

    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="cookie is too large"):
        response.set_cookie("foo", "x" * 50)


def test_max_cookie_size_raised_in_view(app, client):
    @app.route("/")
    def index():
        r = flask.Response("")
        r.max_cookie_size = 10_000
        r.set_cookie("foo", "x" * 5000)
        return r

    with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as caught:
        warnings.simplefilter("always")
        client.get("/")

    assert not any("cookie is too large" in str(w.message) for w in caught)

tasks.title: Autoescape templates with a .j2/.jinja/.jinja2 suffix
tasks.prompt: Templates named with a Jinja extension after the real one, like `page.html.j2`, `page.html.jinja` or `feed.xml.jinja2`, are not autoescaped, because `Flask.select_jinja_autoescape` only looks at the last extension. Make it ignore one trailing `.j2`, `.jinja` or `.jinja2` extension (case-insensitive, like the existing check) and then apply the existing rule (`.html`, `.htm`, `.xml`, `.xhtml`, `.svg`). So `page.html.j2` and `page.HTML.Jinja` return `True`, while `mail.txt.j2`, `page.j2` and `page.jinja` return `False`. `None` still returns `True`, and names without such a suffix behave as before. As a result, rendering `page.html.j2` with `render_template` escapes HTML in variables.

tasks.title: copy_current_request_context should require a request
tasks.prompt: `copy_current_request_context` is documented as needing a request context, and it raises `RuntimeError` when no context is active. Inside a plain app context, though (`with app.app_context():` or a CLI command), it silently accepts the function, and the copied function then runs without a request. Make it raise `RuntimeError` in that case too, with the same message as when no context is active: `'copy_current_request_context' can only be used when a request context is active, such as in a view function.` Behaviour inside a request context is unchanged.

tasks.title: Validate shell context processor return values
tasks.prompt: `app.make_shell_context()` passes whatever each `@app.shell_context_processor` function returns straight to `dict.update`. A processor that returns `None` (for example one that only provides names under some condition) makes `flask shell` crash with an unhelpful `TypeError` from `dict.update`, while values such as a list of pairs are silently accepted. Change it so that a processor returning `None` is skipped, and any return value that is a mapping (any `collections.abc.Mapping`, not only `dict`) is merged as before. Anything else raises `TypeError` with the message `The shell context processor '<name>' must return a dict or None, not <type>.`, where `<name>` is the processor's `__name__` and `<type>` is the type name of the returned value. For example: `The shell context processor 'bad' must return a dict or None, not list.`

tasks.title: Forced tag re-registration should replace the old tag in the order
tasks.prompt: `TaggedJSONSerializer.register(tag_class, force=True)` replaces the entry in `serializer.tags`, but the previously registered tag object stays in `serializer.order`. Tagging uses the first matching tag in `order`, so the old tag keeps being used when dumping and the replacement is ignored. For example, replacing the `" u"` UUID tag with one that writes upper-case hex has no effect on `dumps`. When `force=True` overwrites an existing key, remove the old tag from `order`. If `index` is `None`, the new tag takes the old tag's position in `order`. If `index` is given, the new tag is inserted at that index after the old one has been removed. Registering a new key, and the `KeyError` raised without `force`, stay as they are.
tasks.hidden_test:
from uuid import UUID

import pytest

from flask.json.tag import JSONTag
from flask.json.tag import TaggedJSONSerializer
from flask.json.tag import TagUUID


class TagUUIDUpper(JSONTag):
    __slots__ = ()
    key = " u"

    def check(self, value):
        return isinstance(value, UUID)

    def to_json(self, value):
        return value.hex.upper()

    def to_python(self, value):
        return UUID(value)


VALUE = UUID("abcdef01-2345-6789-abcd-ef0123456789")


def test_forced_replacement_is_used_for_dumps():
    s = TaggedJSONSerializer()
    s.register(TagUUIDUpper, force=True)
    dumped = s.dumps(VALUE)

    assert VALUE.hex.upper() in dumped
    assert VALUE.hex not in dumped
    assert s.loads(dumped) == VALUE


def test_forced_replacement_takes_old_position():
    s = TaggedJSONSerializer()
    old_position = next(
        i for i, tag in enumerate(s.order) if isinstance(tag, TagUUID)
    )
    length = len(s.order)
    s.register(TagUUIDUpper, force=True)

    assert len(s.order) == length
    assert isinstance(s.order[old_position], TagUUIDUpper)
    assert not any(isinstance(tag, TagUUID) for tag in s.order)
    assert isinstance(s.tags[" u"], TagUUIDUpper)


def test_forced_replacement_with_index():
    s = TaggedJSONSerializer()
    length = len(s.order)
    s.register(TagUUIDUpper, force=True, index=0)

    assert len(s.order) == length
    assert isinstance(s.order[0], TagUUIDUpper)
    assert not any(isinstance(tag, TagUUID) for tag in s.order)


def test_register_without_force_still_raises():
    s = TaggedJSONSerializer()

    with pytest.raises(KeyError):
        s.register(TagUUIDUpper)

tasks.title: Return template names in sorted order
tasks.prompt: `app.jinja_env.list_templates()` returns template names in an arbitrary order that changes between runs, which makes tooling output and tests that list templates unstable. Make Flask's template loader return the names from the app and all registered blueprints sorted alphabetically, with each name listed only once even when several loaders provide it.
tasks.hidden_test:
import flask


def test_list_templates_sorted(app):
    names = app.jinja_env.list_templates()

    assert names == sorted(names)
    assert len(names) == len(set(names))
    assert "simple_template.html" in names
    assert "nested/nested.txt" in names


def test_list_templates_with_blueprint_sorted_without_duplicates(app):
    bp = flask.Blueprint("bp", __name__, template_folder="templates")
    app.register_blueprint(bp)
    names = app.jinja_env.list_templates()

    assert names == sorted(set(names))
    assert "simple_template.html" in names
